what: Most of the EU AI Act starts to apply
note: The remainder of the Act takes effect apart from one article, and every member state must by this date have at least one national AI regulatory sandbox operating.

what: Australian national cabinet takes up mandatory data centre standards
note: The Prime Minister said on 15 July he would seek agreement from premiers and chief ministers for mandatory standards covering power supply, connection costs and water efficiency, with legislation to follow early next year.

what: 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting
note: Palau hosts for the first time since 2014, with eighteen member states meeting under the 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent; Forum ICT ministers put artificial intelligence on the regional agenda in July.

what: 4th UNESCO Global Forum on the Ethics of AI
note: Co-hosted by UNESCO and Saudi Arabia under the theme of transforming global cooperation for ethical AI governance; UNESCO says registration details are still to come.

what: 21st Internet Governance Forum
note: Held as a hybrid meeting, so it can be joined without travelling; the theme and the calls for session proposals had not been published at the time of this scan.

what: South Africa reopens public comment on its National AI Policy
note: The April 2026 draft was withdrawn and a revised policy is expected at Cabinet by November 2026 before a fresh comment period opens, so this is a door that has been announced rather than one you can walk through yet.

when_text: May 2027, exact dates not yet set
what: Second session of the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance
note: The first session in Geneva drew criticism from civil society coalitions that women and Indigenous Peoples were insufficiently represented, which makes how this one is convened worth watching.

what: No open consultation found that a member of the public could answer today
note: Every AI consultation traced in this scan had already closed: Ireland in April, Canada in March, the EU transparency guidelines in June and the EU high-risk classification guidelines on 23 July. The next announced opening is South Africa in January 2027.

what: IGF 2026 call for session proposals
where: Online, for the December meeting in Nairobi
note: Governments, civil society, academia, the technical community and the private sector can propose workshops, lightning talks, open forums and Day 0 events, under the published theme Governing the Internet in the Age of Intelligence: Our Shared Responsibility.

what: Australian Senate inquiry into artificial intelligence and data centres
note: The Environment and Communications References Committee takes written submissions from anyone on how well existing rules manage data centre growth and on the effects on communities, industries, the environment, water and energy. The closing date was extended from 26 June to 1 September 2026 and the committee reports on 16 November 2026.

what: Canada consults on AI transparency
note: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada asks how people should be told when they are dealing with an AI system or with AI-generated content, and names individuals and residents, business, researchers, civil society and Indigenous groups including First Nations, Inuit and Métis among those it wants to hear from.

what: New South Wales data centres inquiry due to report
note: The Legislative Council's Public Accountability and Works committee closed submissions on 27 March, held five hearings between May and July on electricity demand, water use, noise, heat and land-use conflict, and is due to report by 30 September 2026.

when_text: January 2027, exact dates not yet set

note: Brunei hosts, following the Hanoi meeting of January 2026 that adopted the Hanoi Digital Declaration and stood up an ASEAN AI Safety Network with its secretariat in Kuala Lumpur.

what: 26th session of the UN Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues
note: Held under the theme of twenty years of the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, at the forum where data centre siting has been raised as a question of consent.

what: 21st Internet Governance Forum
note: Changed since 28 July: the theme is now published as Governing the Internet in the Age of Intelligence: Our Shared Responsibility, and the call for session proposals opened and closes on 31 July 2026. The 28 July line said neither had been published.

what: 4th UNESCO Global Forum on the Ethics of AI
note: Changed since 28 July: registration is now open, through the forum site at gfeai.icaire.org. The 28 July line said registration details were still to come.

what: Three open doors found, correcting the finding of 28 July
note: On 28 July this calendar recorded that no open consultation could be found anywhere. what: UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance submission portal has closed
note: The Global Dialogue site now states that its submission portal is closed. The second session is still listed for May 2027 in New York with no exact dates published. what: EU AI Act transparency rules start to apply
note: Changed since 28 July, and a correction. The 28 July and 21:29 lines both said the remainder of the Act took effect on 2 August 2026 apart from one article, and that every member state had to have a national AI regulatory sandbox operating by that date. The Digital Omnibus on AI entered into force on 27 July 2026, three days after publication in the Official Journal on 24 July, and deferred the Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and Annex I high-risk systems embedded in regulated products to 2 August 2028. Article 50 transparency obligations still apply from 2 August 2026, with a grace period to 2 December 2026 for machine-readable marking on systems already on the market. The source previously cited, artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline, was last updated 1 August 2024 and did not carry the deferral; the entry now cites lewissilkin.com. The sandbox claim is not repeated because it was not verified against the amended text this run.

what: IGF 2026 calls: session proposals, village booths and remote hubs
where: Online, for the December meeting in Nairobi
note: Changed since the 21:29 line, which described a single call for session proposals. Three calls share the 31 July 2026 23:59 UTC deadline: session proposals, IGF Village booths (free, first come first served, with regard to stakeholder and regional balance) and remote hubs. The remote hub call is the one that asks for no travel, and was missing from the earlier line.

what: Second door hunt of 31 July: portals checked and what had already closed
note: Checked beyond AI regulators, following the method fault recorded at 21:29. Closed: UNESCO Global Forum research and panel proposals (closed 18 July 2026); OECD Governing with Artificial Intelligence global call (closed 20 March 2026); the Citizen Lab People's Consultation on AI (closed 15 March 2026); the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance submission portal; the EU AI Act Advisory Forum call for applications (closed 14 September 2025); the UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI nominations (closed 31 October 2025). No live consultation found on industry.gov.au despite an Office of AI standing up in the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet on 15 July 2026, which is worth re-checking. The Oireachtas pre-legislative scrutiny consultation on the Irish AI Bill could not be read: aph.gov.au and oireachtas.ie both return 403 to the fetch tool, so both were verified through secondary reporting instead. Senate inquiry confirmed: referred 13 May 2026, submissions close 1 September 2026, reports 16 November 2026.

what: Spain consults before drafting a law on generative AI and performers
note: The Ministry of Labour and Social Economy opened a prior public consultation on 31 July 2026, closing 14 August 2026, ahead of an organic law on the use of generative AI on the image and voice of people working in the performing arts, audiovisual and music, and the technical and auxiliary workers alongside them. The Council of State advised that an organic law is required because generated content can reach rights protected by article 18 of the Spanish constitution. The provision was removed from Real Decreto 607/2026 as a result. A technical commission with unions and sectoral bodies is proposed to monitor use.

what: United Kingdom call for evidence on data regulation in the age of AI
note: Opened 15 July 2026 and closes at 11:59pm on 9 September 2026. Asks for practical examples of how personal and non-personal data regulation interacts with AI and other data-intensive technologies, what is working, where uncertainty remains and where friction is expected. Open to businesses, researchers, civil society and individuals.

what: Uruguay consults on children, adolescents, digital environments and AI
note: Run by the Uruguayan parliament with the national honorary consultative council on the rights of children and adolescents, AGESIC, Ceibal, UNICEF and UNDP. Published phases: preparation and co-design 15 May to 23 June; open consultation and multi-stakeholder exchange 23 June to 10 September; systematisation, analysis and validation 10 September to 20 October; final report 30 November 2026. The open digital consultation closes 10 September. Separate sittings are held for children and adolescents in formats matched to age, context, language and progressive autonomy. Found by searching in Spanish; absent from every English-language search run this scan.

what: United Kingdom all-party parliamentary group on data centres taking written evidence
note: Inquiry titled Unlocking the UK Data Centre Growth Opportunity, chaired by Chris Curtis MP, written evidence by 17:00 on 25 September 2026 to info@datacentresappg.co.uk, three oral evidence sessions between September and November on energy infrastructure and international competitiveness, investment and planning, and innovation and sustainability, recommendations December 2026. Those invited are named as operators and developers, investors, energy suppliers, network operators, water providers, consultancies, local authorities, technology providers, trade associations, environmental groups and academic institutions. Individuals are not named.

what: ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26)
note: The highest policy-making conference of the International Telecommunication Union, held every four years, with all 194 member states setting the union policies, direction and activities and electing its leadership. Agenda includes global connectivity, internet governance, child online protection and the governance of emerging technologies including artificial intelligence. Decisions run to 2030.

what: IGF 2026 calls: session proposals, village booths and remote hubs
where: Online, for the December meeting in Nairobi
note: Changed since 31 July: the deadline was extended from 31 July 2026 to Sunday 2 August 2026 at 23:59 UTC. note: Changed since 28 July, when this was recorded as May 2027 with exact dates not set. what: United States, comment period on adding AI questions to the American Time Use Survey
where: United States, by email to the BLS clearance officer
note: The Bureau of Labor Statistics proposes asking people whether they use AI tools, for what tasks, and how that use sits against work, education, household responsibilities and leisure. The bureau states that no federal survey currently links an individual's AI use to a detailed record of their activities. Questions are to be fielded from January 2027 for two years, so the comment period is when the wording can still be changed. Published in the Federal Register on 10 July 2026, document 2026-13928, a 60 day period under the Paperwork Reduction Act.

when_text: Closes 8 September 2026, previously recorded as 9 September
what: Correction: the ATUS comment date is 8 September, and the entry should not have been dropped
note: The 12:34 scan on 11 August found this notice, recorded the closing date as 9 September 2026, and then dropped it from the page for want of a readable source, because federalregister.gov returns a block page to the fetch tool and the Justia mirror returns HTTP 403. Both facts were wrong in effect. The date is 8 September 2026, and the source is readable through the same site's JSON interface at federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents/2026-13928.json, which returned comments_close_on 2026-09-08 without difficulty. Method note for later runs: when a government page blocks the fetch tool, try its machine-readable interface before recording the entry as unverifiable. A blocked page is not a closed door.

what: Cameroon Internet Governance Forum 2026, on moving from fragmentation to interoperability and making data the foundation of public digital infrastructure, covering data ownership, storage, sharing and protection, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and digital divides, with a side meeting on women, data and artificial intelligence
note: Organised by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications. Civil society named among participants. Dates confirmed against the AITN report after the Digital Business Africa page did not carry them.

what: A Texas House committee meets on whether special rules are needed to protect residents' water and electricity from data centre demand. Data centres in Texas do not report water use and need no permit from the state environmental commission to draw groundwater. The Laredo representative Richard Pena Raymond has asked the Governor for a special session and a moratorium on further approvals until impacts are assessed
note: Surfaced on a Spanish-language search of Mexican border coverage, invisible to the English queries run the same day.

what: Texas House State Affairs Committee hears invited and public testimony on data centre development

what: Mexico's regional forums on children, adolescents, digital platforms and artificial intelligence
where: Nuevo Leon, then Chiapas, then Guerrero, Mexico

They follow talks already run by the education ministry in the metropolitan region, Baja California Sur and Jalisco. Conclusions are intended to go to the Congress of the Union as a bill.

what: Charlotte holds six public sessions on what should replace its data centre moratorium
where: Charlotte, North Carolina, United States, and online

what: Spain consults on the 2026 update of its national Digital Decade roadmap

note: Opened 20 July 2026 by the Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service, closing 18 September 2026. what: Correction: the twelve entry cap is abolished and the five entries held off the page for space are restored
note: Luke pulled this up directly. Runs on 11 and 15 August read the routine's 'three to twelve entries' house rule as a hard ceiling and evicted qualifying entries to stay under it, leaving them in this file with a line on the page saying they were held off for space. Restored to the page: 4th UNESCO Global Forum on the Ethics of AI, 14 to 17 September 2026, Riyadh; Pan African AI Summit, 22 and 23 September 2026, Accra; ITU Plenipotentiary Conference, 9 to 27 November 2026, Doha; 21st Internet Governance Forum, 14 to 18 December 2026, Nairobi; 26th session of the UN Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues, 10 to 21 May 2027, New York. Seventeen entries now, nine of them doors. The rule in the routine has been rewritten to say there is no upper limit and that nothing qualifying is ever removed to make room. The original rule was aimed at padding, meaning do not invent filler to reach a number, and was never meant to evict real meetings. Still held from earlier runs and worth reinstating when confirmed: South Africa's expected comment period in January 2027, the 7th ASEAN Digital Ministers Meeting in January 2027, and the second UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance on 3 and 4 May 2027. The New South Wales data centres inquiry stays off on its own merits, because a committee reporting date is not a place a person can attend.

what: Denton City Council votes on whether to set public hearings for a data centre moratorium
note: A council majority of four to three directed staff in early August 2026 to prepare a 90-day moratorium on data centre approvals and amendments to the Denton development code, after the municipal utility warned the grid is near capacity. The 18 August vote sets the hearing dates. If passed, the first public hearing could occur as early as 22 September 2026 and the second as early as 27 October 2026, with a possible moratorium ruling on 2 December 2026. Those three dates are tentative and contingent on the 18 August vote. A moratorium requires a supermajority.

what: Hendersonville City Council public hearing on a data centre moratorium of up to twelve months
note: The council set the hearing at its 22 July 2026 meeting. The moratorium would halt city approvals including building, zoning and special use permits for any data centre for up to twelve months while the city updates its code. City Attorney Angie Beeker told the council the existing ordinance is outdated and not prepared to address data centres, citing water use, electricity use and noise. Mayor Barbara Volk has indicated the city is considering size caps, minimum distances and sound barriers. No data centre is currently proposed in Hendersonville. The reporting gives the date but not the starting time or the room.

when_text: Opened 12 August 2026, closes 13 October 2026 at 11:59pm Eastern
what: NIST request for information on modernising the National Vulnerability Database in the age of artificial intelligence
where: United States, online through the federal rulemaking portal at regulations.gov, docket NIST-2026-0100
note: The National Institute of Standards and Technology seeks input on opportunities, challenges and priorities for modernising the NVD, the public catalogue of known software flaws that security tools read from. Areas named include improving vulnerability data quality, governance and machine-readability; how AI-enabled tools can be integrated into software development to identify and address vulnerabilities earlier while retaining human oversight, transparency and data quality; and capabilities, services and performance metrics for the NVD over the next five years. The RFI follows a sharp rise in reported vulnerabilities attributed in part to AI-assisted discovery outpacing the catalogue.

what: Fort Worth holds two public hearings before adopting a 90-day data centre moratorium
note: Council voted unanimously on 11 August 2026 to initiate the moratorium process and create a Data Center and Infrastructure Committee. Published timetable: notice of first public hearing 9 October 2026; committee presents studies and report in work session 3 November 2026; first public hearing 10 November 2026; notice of second public hearing 13 November 2026; second public hearing 5 January 2027; first reading of the proposed ordinance 12 January 2027; second reading and adoption by supermajority 16 February 2027; moratorium ends 17 May 2027. Residents may speak at both public hearings. During the pause, staff are to evaluate noise impacts, effects on water supplies, long-term water availability, land-use compatibility and associated infrastructure. Projects with already-submitted or approved zoning applications are exempt.

what: EU AI Act: marking grace period ends and two new prohibited practices begin
note: Generative AI systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 were given a transitional period until 2 December 2026 to comply with the machine-readable marking and detection obligation for synthetic content. From the same date, two practices added to Article 5 by the Digital Omnibus on AI are prohibited: AI systems designed to generate non-consensual intimate imagery, and AI systems that generate child sexual abuse material. The Digital Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, entered into force on 27 July 2026 and deferred stand-alone Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and embedded Annex I systems to 2 August 2028.

when_text: January 2027, exact date not yet set
what: 7th ASEAN Digital Ministers Meeting
note: Brunei hosts the digital ministers of the ten ASEAN member states and dialogue partners. The 6th ADGMIN adopted an expanded ASEAN framework on AI governance and ethics covering generative AI and set work in train on a regional AI safety network. what: Second session of the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance
note: Established by General Assembly resolution as a recurring annual mechanism open to all member states and to stakeholders including civil society. The first session was held in Geneva on 6 and 7 July 2026, alongside the WSIS Forum and the AI for Good Global Summit. The second session is scheduled in New York alongside the Multistakeholder Forum on Science, Technology and Innovation for the Global Goals. The FAQ states that registration arrangements and requirements for future annual Dialogues will be published on the Dialogue website when available; no submission window is open at present. Joint secretariat: ITU, UNESCO, ODET and EOSG. Reinstated from the list earlier runs held back pending confirmation. Note the proximity to the 26th session of the UN Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues in the same city on 10 to 21 May 2027.

what: South Africa's expected January 2027 AI policy comment period is removed from the standing list
note: Earlier runs held South Africa's expected comment period in January 2027 on the reinstatement list. what: Prince William County reheard public hearings on the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District amendment (DPA2026-00006)
where: Prince William County, Virginia, United States
note: The Board of County Supervisors initiated the amendment on 9 June to reduce and redefine the overlay district boundaries, limiting it to parcels meeting one of five county-defined eligibility pathways and eliminating by-right data centre development. The planning commission is to rehear the entirety of the proposal on 9 September because community mailers gave improper public notice of the first hearing. An email from the county planning director dated 23 July states staff anticipate presenting the case to the Board of County Supervisors at a public hearing on 22 September. Residents may speak at both. The rehearing itself is the Q9 point: a hearing set aside because the people who should have been told were not told properly.

what: Southport Board of Aldermen public hearing on a data centre moratorium of up to fifteen months
note: The Board of Aldermen voted unanimously on 13 August 2026 to move forward with scheduling the public hearing, following a July vote by the town planning board requesting the moratorium. The moratorium would halt approvals for data centre projects while city staff develop land use standards. Reporting gives the date but not the starting time or the room, so the board agenda needs checking before attending. Third North Carolina municipality on the page taking this step within weeks, alongside Charlotte and Hendersonville.

what: Mississauga council to approve the interim control bylaw giving effect to its AI data centre moratorium
note: Councillors voted unanimously in July 2026 for a moratorium of one year, and up to two, on new AI data centre developments, after public deputations at the council meeting. The interim control bylaw comes forward for council approval on 16 September. Staff are also to bring an interim report to council later in the year setting out the study scope, the consultation strategy and review timelines, so the date on which residents are formally consulted is not yet published; that interim report is the thing to watch. A proponent is expected to appeal. Reported as the first Ontario city to pause new AI data centres.

what: Northern Ireland public consultation on its draft Artificial Intelligence Strategy
note: The Executive Office opened an eight-week consultation on 12 August 2026. The draft strategy sets out a vision for the responsible, ethical and fair adoption of AI across the public sector, built on eight principles: human oversight, accountability and redress, data governance, technical safety and security, fairness and transparency, sustainability, societal benefit, and training and literacy. It states AI should augment human capabilities rather than replace them and that human decision-making is preserved. The First Minister said the office wants to hear directly from people, communities and organisations so the strategy is shaped by those most impacted, which places individuals inside the invitation. Responses go through the Executive Office consultations page.

what: South Australian Royal Commission into Artificial Intelligence commences
note: Announced by Premier Peter Malinauskas on 11 August 2026. Commences 1 October 2026, final report to government no later than 1 July 2027. Three commissioners to be appointed with expertise in current AI technologies, labour and employment, and economics and business; cost put at more than three million dollars. Scope covers effects on work, the creative industries, education, health, industry and public services. Expected to take evidence and submissions from business, industry bodies, unions, technology developers, academics, independent experts and creative industry representatives, but no submission window has been published, so it is logged as a meeting and not a door. Two caveats recorded at first entry: the Premier said terms of reference would be confirmed within about six weeks of the announcement, so scope was still being drafted; and he stated infrastructure such as data centres is excluded, which places the buildings and their water and power demand outside a state inquiry into AI's effects on that state.

what: Next state-level global AI summit held off the page: Geneva 2027 has a city and a year but no month
note: Swiss President Guy Parmelin announced at the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi on 19 February 2026 that Switzerland will host the next global summit on AI in Geneva in 2027, co-hosted with ITU and UN partners, with the United Arab Emirates to host in 2028. One secondary source gave 21 and 22 June 2027; this could not be confirmed against digitalswitzerland or swissinfo, both of which give the year only. Held off the page under the rule that an entry needs a real date from the source, a month at minimum. Recheck when a month is published. Preparatory events named for 2026: the Digital Summit in May and the digitalswitzerland forum in September.

what: Method note: Spanish-language searches returned 2023 and 2024 consultation cycles presented as current
note: Two apparently strong open doors turned out to be old cycles resurfacing. A consultation on revising Uruguay's National AI Strategy and creating a National Data Strategy, described in search results as running 16 September to 7 October, is the 2024 cycle: the process page on plataformaparticipacionciudadana.gub.uy gives phases from May 2023 to October 2024 with the public consultation 16 September to 6 October 2024. The Xunta de Galicia consultation on a future Galician AI law is the 2023 cycle, open 15 September to 15 October 2023. Both were dropped. Rule for future runs: every Spanish and Portuguese language consultation hit must be opened and the year read off the source page before it goes on the calendar, because the search layer strips the year from these pages.
